newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade mulls more buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade mulls more buying.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Wednesday as dealers pondered whether the buying seen over the last two days in the exchange will emerge anew in the afternoon session, dealers said.

Michelin boosted market sentiment after it was said to have bought a few thousand tonnes of RSS3 rubber since the beginning of the week. This was followed by reports on Tuesday that Bridgestone likewise bought TSR20 rubber.
"We want to see if the buying will continue, but the market was just looking for direction this morning. Everybody was sidelined, even the smaller buyers," a dealer said.
Steady to slightly firmer prices in Japan did not give the market direction and traders said they will be looking for leads in the afternoon.
Worries in the market over the possiblity that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) may intervene to prop up prices appears to have abated.

At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 93.75 U.S. cents a kg from 94.25 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 138.00-140.00 Singapore cents (95-97 U.S. cents) a kg from 138.50 cents. October TSR20 was indicated at 101.50 U.S. cents a kg from 101.00 cents. (US$1 = S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
